# moltis
## HarnessBench adapter
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from harnessbench.adapters.base import BaseAdapter
from harnessbench.models import AdapterRunContext, AdapterRunResult
from harnessbench.usage_proxy import register_routes


def _project_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _resolve_project_path(raw: str | Path) -> Path:
    p = Path(os.path.expanduser(str(raw)))
    if not p.is_absolute():
        p = _project_root() / p
    return p.resolve()


def _loads_toml(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
        import tomllib

        return tomllib.loads(text)
    import tomli

    return tomli.loads(text)


def _load_user_config(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if suffix == ".json":
        data = json.loads(raw)
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
    if suffix in (".toml",):
        return _loads_toml(raw)
    if suffix in (".yaml", ".yml"):
        try:
            import yaml  # type: ignore
        except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{path} requires PyYAML; install pyyaml or use .toml/.json") from exc
        loaded = yaml.safe_load(raw)
        return loaded if isinstance(loaded, dict) else {}
    # Guess by content
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        pass
    return _loads_toml(raw)


def _merge_providers_for_proxy(
    data: dict[str, Any],
    proxy_base_url: str,
    routes_file: Path | None,
) -> None:
    if not proxy_base_url or routes_file is None:
        return
    providers = data.get("providers")
    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
        return
    skip = {"offered", "show_legacy_models"}
    routes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for name, cfg in providers.items():
        if name in skip or not isinstance(cfg, dict):
            continue
        upstream = str(cfg.get("base_url") or cfg.get("url") or "").strip()
        if not upstream:
            continue
        prefix = f"/moltis/{name}"
        routes[prefix] = {
            "framework": "moltis",
            "provider": str(name),
            "upstream": upstream,
        }
        cfg["base_url"] = f"{proxy_base_url.rstrip('/')}{prefix}"
    if routes:
        register_routes(routes_file, routes)


def _write_merged_config(data: dict[str, Any], out_path: Path) -> None:
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


class MoltisAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    """Run Moltis via `moltis agent` with isolated config/data dirs (HarnessBench)."""

    name = "moltis"

    def run(self, ctx: AdapterRunContext) -> AdapterRunResult:
        command = str(ctx.model_config.get("command") or "moltis")
        user_config_raw = str(ctx.model_config.get("user_config") or os.path.expanduser("~/.config/moltis/moltis.toml"))
        user_config = _resolve_project_path(user_config_raw)
        if not user_config.is_file():
            return AdapterRunResult(ok=False, stderr=f"missing Moltis source config: {user_config}")

        isolated_home = ctx.sandbox
        moltis_config_dir = isolated_home / ".config" / "moltis"
        moltis_config_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        merged_cfg = moltis_config_dir / "moltis.json"

        data = _load_user_config(user_config)
        _merge_providers_for_proxy(
            data,
            proxy_base_url=str(ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_URL") or ""),
            routes_file=Path(ctx.env["HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES"]) if ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES") else None,
        )
        _write_merged_config(data, merged_cfg)

        extra = [str(x) for x in (ctx.model_config.get("args") or [])]
        cmd: list[str] = [command, *extra, "agent", "--message", ctx.prompt, "--session-id", ctx.session_id, "--timeout", str(ctx.timeout_sec)]
        model_override = ctx.model_config.get("model")
        if model_override:
            cmd.extend(["--model", str(model_override)])

        env = os.environ.copy()
        env.update(ctx.env)
        env["HOME"] = str(isolated_home)
        env["MOLTIS_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(moltis_config_dir)
        env["MOLTIS_DATA_DIR"] = str(ctx.workspace.resolve())

        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=str(ctx.sandbox),
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=ctx.timeout_sec,
            env=env,
            check=False,
        )
        return AdapterRunResult(
            ok=completed.returncode == 0,
            command=cmd,
            stdout=completed.stdout,
            stderr=completed.stderr,
            metadata={
                "returncode": completed.returncode,
                "moltis_config_dir": str(moltis_config_dir),
                "merged_config_path": str(merged_cfg),
                "source_user_config_path": str(user_config),
                "isolated_home": str(isolated_home),
                "workspace": str(ctx.workspace),
                # HarnessBench usage_summary resolves session/jsonl under this root (see runner._collect_usage_summary).
                "state_dir": str(ctx.workspace.resolve()),
            },
        )

## Upstream README
<div align="center">

<a href="https://moltis.org"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moltis-org/moltis/main/website/favicon.svg" alt="Moltis" width="64"></a>

# Moltis — A secure persistent personal agent server in Rust

One binary — sandboxed, secure, yours.

[![CI](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/moltis-org/moltis/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/moltis-org/moltis)
[![CodSpeed](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://codspeed.io/badge.json&style=flat&label=CodSpeed)](https://codspeed.io/moltis-org/moltis)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-1.91%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1469505370169933837?color=5865F2&label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/XnmrepsXp5)

[Installation](#installation) • [Comparison](#comparison) • [Architecture](#architecture--crate-map) • [Security](#security) • [Features](#features) • [How It Works](#how-it-works) • [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

---

Moltis recently hit [the front page of Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46993587). Please [open an issue](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/issues) for any friction at all. I'm focused on making Moltis excellent.

**Secure by design** — Your keys never leave your machine. Every command runs in a sandboxed container, never on your host.

**Your hardware** — Runs on a Mac Mini, a Raspberry Pi, or any server you own. One Rust binary, no Node.js, no npm, no runtime.

**Full-featured** — Voice, memory, cross-session recall, automatic edit checkpoints, scheduling, Telegram, Signal, Discord, browser automation, MCP servers, SSH or node-backed remote exec, managed deploy keys with host pinning in the web UI, a live Settings → Tools inventory, Cursor-compatible project context, and context-file threat scanning — all built-in. No plugin marketplace to get supply-chain attacked through.

**Auditable** — The agent runner and model interface fit in ~7.5K lines, with providers in ~19K more. The Rust workspace is ~270K lines across 59 modular crates you can audit independently, with 470+ Rust files containing tests. Unsafe code is isolated to FFI and precompiled runtime boundaries, not the core agent loop.

## Installation

```bash
# One-liner install script (macOS / Linux)
curl -fsSL https://www.moltis.org/install.sh | sh

# macOS / Linux via Homebrew
brew install moltis-org/tap/moltis

# Docker (multi-arch: amd64/arm64)
docker pull ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest

# Or build from source
cargo install moltis --git https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis
```

## Comparison

| | OpenClaw | Hermes Agent | **Moltis** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary stack | TypeScript + Swift/Kotlin companion apps | Python + TypeScript TUI/web surfaces | **Rust** |
| Runtime | Node.js + npm/pnpm/bun | Python + uv/pip, optional Node UI pieces | **Single Rust binary** |
| Local checkout size\* | ~1.1M app LoC | ~152K app LoC | **~270K Rust LoC** |
| Architecture | Broad gateway, channel, node, and app ecosystem | CLI/gateway agent with learning loop and research tooling | **Persistent personal agent server with modular crates** |
| Crates/modules | npm packages, extensions, apps | Python packages, plugins, tools, TUI | **59 Rust workspace crates** |
| Sandbox/backends | App-level permissions, browser/node tools | Local, Docker, SSH, Daytona, Singularity, Modal | **Docker/Podman + Apple Container + WASM** |
| Auth/access | Pairing and local gateway controls | CLI and messaging gateway setup | **Password + Passkey + API keys + Vault** |
| Voice I/O | Voice wake and talk modes | Voice memo transcription | **Built-in STT + TTS providers** |
| MCP | Plugin/integration support | MCP integration | **stdio + HTTP/SSE** |
| Skills | Bundled, managed, and workspace skills | Self-improving skills and Skills Hub support | **Bundled/workspace skills + autonomous improvement + OpenClaw import** |
| Memory/RAG | Plugin-backed memory and context engine | Agent-curated memory, session search, user modeling | **SQLite + FTS + vector memory** |

\* LoC measured with `tokei`, excluding `node_modules`, generated build output, `dist`, and `target`.

> [Full comparison in the docs →](https://docs.moltis.org/comparison.html)

## Architecture — Crate Map

Current Rust workspace: ~270K LoC across 59 crates. The table below groups the main crates by role so the architecture stays scannable.

**Core runtime**:

| Crate | LoC | Role |
|-------|-----|------|
| `moltis-gateway` | 37.4K | HTTP/WS server, RPC, auth, startup wiring |
| `moltis-tools` | 37.0K | Tool execution, sandboxing, WASM tools |
| `moltis-providers` | 18.9K | LLM provider implementations |
| `moltis-agents` | 14.5K | Agent loop, streaming, prompt assembly |
| `moltis-chat` | 14.2K | Chat engine, agent orchestration |
| `moltis-config` | 10.3K | Configuration, validation |
| `moltis-httpd` | 9.9K | HTTP server primitives and middleware |
| `moltis` (CLI) | 4.7K | Entry point, CLI commands |
| `moltis-sessions` | 3.5K | Session persistence |
| `moltis-common` | 1.5K | Shared utilities |
| `moltis-service-traits` | 1.2K | Shared service interfaces |
| `moltis-protocol` | 0.7K | Wire protocol types |

**Feature and integration crates**:

| Category | Crates | Combined LoC |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| Channels | `moltis-telegram`, `moltis-whatsapp`, `moltis-signal`, `moltis-discord`, `moltis-msteams`, `moltis-matrix`, `moltis-slack`, `moltis-nostr`, `moltis-channels` | 34.0K |
| Web and APIs | `moltis-web`, `moltis-graphql`, `moltis-webhooks` | 10.8K |
| Extensibility | `moltis-mcp`, `moltis-mcp-agent-bridge`, `moltis-skills`, `moltis-plugins` | 11.5K |
| Memory and context | `moltis-memory`, `moltis-qmd`, `moltis-code-index`, `moltis-projects` | 11.7K |
| Voice and browser | `moltis-voice`, `moltis-browser` | 9.2K |
| Auth and security | `moltis-auth`, `moltis-oauth`, `moltis-vault`, `moltis-secret-store`, `moltis-network-filter`, `moltis-tls` | 8.5K |
| Scheduling and automation | `moltis-cron`, `moltis-caldav`, `moltis-auto-reply` | 4.7K |
| Setup and import | `moltis-provider-setup`, `moltis-openclaw-import`, `moltis-onboarding` | 11.7K |
| Native and node hosts | `moltis-swift-bridge`, `moltis-node-host`, `moltis-courier` | 5.7K |
| WASM tools | `moltis-wasm-precompile`, `moltis-wasm-calc`, `moltis-wasm-web-fetch`, `moltis-wasm-web-search` | 1.4K |
| Supporting crates | `moltis-media`, `moltis-metrics`, `moltis-tailscale`, `moltis-routing`, `moltis-canvas`, `moltis-schema-export`, `benchmarks` | 2.1K |

Use `--no-default-features --features lightweight` for constrained devices (Raspberry Pi, etc.).

## Security

- **Small unsafe surface** — core agent/gateway code stays safe Rust; unsafe is isolated to Swift FFI, local model wrappers, and precompiled WASM boundaries
- **Sandboxed execution** — Docker + Apple Container, per-session isolation
- **Secret handling** — `secrecy::Secret`, zeroed on drop, redacted from tool output
- **Authentication** — password + passkey (WebAuthn), rate-limited, per-IP throttle
- **SSRF protection** — DNS-resolved, blocks loopback/private/link-local
- **Origin validation** — rejects cross-origin WebSocket upgrades
- **Hook gating** — `BeforeToolCall` hooks can inspect/block any tool invocation
- **Supply chain integrity** — [artifact attestations](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/attestations), Sigstore keyless signing, GPG signing (YubiKey), SHA-256/SHA-512 checksums

See [Security Architecture](https://docs.moltis.org/security.html) for details.
Verify releases with `gh attestation verify <artifact> -R moltis-org/moltis` or see [Release Verification](https://docs.moltis.org/release-verification.html).

## Features

- **Reasoning Defaults** - Configurable default thinking effort for model-less and new main sessions, with explicit per-session Off or level overrides
- **AI Gateway** — Multi-provider LLM support (OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Local), streaming responses, agent loop with sub-agent delegation, session modes, parallel tool execution
- **Communication** — Web UI with command-palette agent prompts and Markdown copy/export, Telegram, Signal, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Slack with native live tool cards, Nostr DMs + NIP-29 group chat (incl. Block's Buzz channels), API access, voice I/O (8 TTS + 7 STT providers), mobile PWA with push notifications
- **Memory & Recall** — Per-agent memory workspaces, embeddings-powered long-term memory, hybrid vector + full-text search, session persistence with auto-compaction, cross-session recall, Cursor-compatible project context, context-file safety scanning
- **Managed Files** - Authenticated nested file management in Settings, with an agent-advertised host path and independent read-only-by-default mounts for Docker, Podman, and Apple Container sandboxes
- **Safer Agent Editing** — Automatic checkpoints before built-in skill and memory mutations, restore tooling, session branching
- **Extensibility** — MCP servers (stdio + HTTP/SSE), skill system, 15 lifecycle hook events with circuit breaker, destructive command guard
- **Agent Client Protocol** — drives external ACP agents (`codex-acp`, `claude-agent-acp`, Cursor), and serves Moltis to ACP clients over stdio via `moltis acp`
- **Security** — Encryption-at-rest vault (XChaCha20-Poly1305 + Argon2id), password + passkey + API key auth, sandbox isolation, SSRF/CSWSH protection
- **Operations** — Cron scheduling, durable local CalDAV, Gmail, Himalaya email, and reusable Slack/Discord/Matrix/Teams message datasets, provider-specific read-only agent tools, fast full-text search, JSONL/Markdown projections, agent instrumentation (Langfuse for LLM traces, OTLP for Grafana/Datadog), Prometheus metrics, cloud deploy (Fly.io, DigitalOcean), Tailscale integration, managed SSH deploy keys, host-pinned remote targets, live tool inventory in Settings, and CLI/web remote-exec doctor flows

## How It Works

Moltis is a **local-first persistent agent server** — a single Rust binary that
sits between you and multiple LLM providers, keeps durable session state, and
can meet you across channels without handing your data to a cloud relay.

```
┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐
│   Web UI    │  │  Telegram   │  │  Discord    │
└──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘
       │                │                │
       └────────┬───────┴────────┬───────┘
                │   WebSocket    │
                ▼                ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
        │          Gateway Server         │
        │   (Axum · HTTP · WS · Auth)     │
        ├─────────────────────────────────┤
        │        Chat Service             │
        │  ┌───────────┐ ┌─────────────┐  │
        │  │   Agent   │ │    Tool     │  │
        │  │   Runner  │◄┤   Registry  │  │
        │  └─────┬─────┘ └─────────────┘  │
        │        │                        │
        │  ┌─────▼─────────────────────┐  │
        │  │    Provider Registry      │  │
        │  │  Multiple providers       │  │
        │  │  (Codex · Copilot · Local)│  │
        │  └───────────────────────────┘  │
        ├─────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Sessions  │ Memory  │  Hooks   │
        │  (JSONL)   │ (SQLite)│ (events) │
        └─────────────────────────────────┘
                       │
               ┌───────▼───────┐
               │    Sandbox    │
               │ Docker/Apple  │
               │  Container    │
               └───────────────┘
```

See [Quickstart](https://docs.moltis.org/quickstart.html) for gateway startup, message flow, sessions, and memory details.

## Getting Started

### Build & Run

Requires [just](https://github.com/casey/just) (command runner) and Node.js (for Tailwind CSS).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis.git
cd moltis
just build-css                  # Build Tailwind CSS for the web UI
just build-release              # Build in release mode
cargo run --release --bin moltis
```

For a full release build including WASM sandbox tools:

```bash
just build-release-with-wasm    # Builds WASM artifacts + release binary
cargo run --release --bin moltis
```

Open `https://moltis.localhost:3000`. On first run, a setup code is printed to
the terminal — enter it in the web UI to set your password or register a passkey.

Optional flags: `--config-dir /path/to/config --data-dir /path/to/data`

### Docker

```bash
# Docker / OrbStack
docker run -d \
  --name moltis \
  -p 13131:13131 \
  -p 13132:13132 \
  -p 1455:1455 \
  -v moltis-config:/home/moltis/.config/moltis \
  -v moltis-data:/home/moltis/.moltis \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest
```

Open `https://localhost:13131` and complete the setup. For unattended Docker
deployments, set `MOLTIS_PASSWORD`, `MOLTIS_PROVIDER`, and `MOLTIS_API_KEY`
before first boot to skip the setup wizard. See [Docker docs](https://docs.moltis.org/docker.html)
for Podman, OrbStack, TLS trust, and persistence details.

### Cloud Deployment

| Provider | Deploy |
|----------|--------|
| DigitalOcean | [![Deploy to DO](https://www.deploytodo.com/do-btn-blue.svg)](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/apps/new?repo=https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/tree/main) |

**Fly.io** (CLI):

```bash
fly launch --image ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest
fly secrets set MOLTIS_PASSWORD="your-password"
```

All cloud configs use `--no-tls` because the provider handles TLS termination.
See [Cloud Deploy docs](https://docs.moltis.org/cloud-deploy.html) for details.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-111-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-112-[Managed Files](managed-files.md) are one shared tree at `<data_dir>/files`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:113:not a per-session store. The deliberate product policy is that **all agent
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:114:sessions, including channel-originated sessions, can read that tree whenever
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:115:their available tools and sandbox mount permit it**. Channel sessions remain
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:116:subject to channel authorization and tool policy, but there is no additional
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-117-Files-level partition after access is permitted.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-118-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-119-This is especially important for health information and other private data. Do
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:120:not upload such files unless every agent session and channel operator with tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-121-access may read them. To prevent local container sandboxes from seeing the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-122-tree, set:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-123-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-124-```toml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:125:[tools.exec.sandbox]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-126-managed_files_mount = "none"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-127-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-379-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:380:The `web_fetch` tool resolves DNS and blocks requests to private IP ranges

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-382-forgery attacks.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-527-   `--no-tls` (or `MOLTIS_NO_TLS=true`) in this mode.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-528-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:529:   If your browser is being redirected to `https://<domain>:13131`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-530-   Moltis TLS is still enabled while your proxy upstream is plain HTTP.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-531-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-571-- Moltis runs with `MOLTIS_BEHIND_PROXY=true`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-572-- For standard edge TLS termination, Moltis runs with `--no-tls`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:573:- NPM preserves browser host/origin context
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-574-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-575-Use this in NPM's **Advanced** field:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-604-- If users move from one hostname to another, old passkeys for the old host
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-605-  will not authenticate on the new host.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:606:- If a proxy rewrites `Host` and does not preserve browser host context,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-607-  passkey routes can fail with "no passkey config for this hostname".
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-608-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:700:## Release Signing and Verification
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-701-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-702-All release artifacts are signed with three independent methods:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-703-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:704:1. **[GitHub artifact attestations](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/attestations)**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-705-   (automated in CI) — cryptographic provenance records tied to the repository,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-706-   workflow, and commit SHA; provides SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2 guarantees;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:707:   verifiable with `gh attestation verify`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-708-2. **Sigstore keyless signing** (automated in CI) — proves the artifact was
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-709-   built by the `moltis-org/moltis` GitHub Actions pipeline; recorded in
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-714-Checksums (SHA-256 and SHA-512) are generated for every artifact.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-715-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md:716:See [Release Verification](release-verification.md) for detailed verification
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/security.md-717-instructions, artifact file extensions, and maintainer signing workflow.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md:212:cannot yet prove Teams topology from its conversation ID, so tools, private
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md:213:owner context, `/sh`, location updates, and privileged commands are denied even
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-214-for configured operators. Use the authenticated web UI for privileged work.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-400-### Bot doesn't respond
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-401-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md:402:- Verify the **Messaging endpoint** in the Azure Portal matches your Moltis webhook URL
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-403-- Check that `app_id` and `app_password` are correct
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-404-- Ensure your server is reachable from the internet over HTTPS
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-429-- Moltis returns `202 Accepted` immediately to prevent Teams retry timeouts.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-430-  If you see duplicates, check for multiple Moltis instances pointing at the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md:431:  same webhook URL, or verify the deduplication middleware is working
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-432-  (duplicate activity IDs are filtered automatically)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/teams.md-433-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-122-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-123-By default, Telegram group chats, guest DMs (messages from non-operators), and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:124:unknown chat kinds receive no tools. As with Slack, MCP tools require **both**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-125-account settings below:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-126-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-128-[channels.telegram.my-bot]

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:130:untrusted_tools = "policy"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-131-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-132-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-133-`untrusted_audience = "trusted"` makes MCP, WASM, and other trusted-audience
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:134:tools eligible. `untrusted_tools = "policy"` removes the blanket name denial
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:135:and lets the [tool policy layers](tool-policy.md) decide which tools are
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:136:available. Neither setting alone enables MCP tools, and a policy allow list
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-137-alone cannot bypass the default ceiling.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-138-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-140-These settings apply to every turn outside an operator direct chat for this
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-141-bot account, including guest DMs, not just the group you intend to enable.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:142:Without restrictive policies, those turns can reach every tool allowed by the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-143-remaining policy layers. Set `group_policy = "allowlist"` with a narrow
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-144-`group_allowlist`, restrict DM access with `dm_policy` and `allowlist` (or
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:149:For TOML-managed accounts, restrict tools for each enabled chat type with
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:150:`tools.groups.<chat_type>` policies, including `private` for guest DMs. For
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:151:UI-managed accounts, database-backed `tools.groups` policies are not currently
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-152-part of runtime policy resolution: configure a restrictive global or provider
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-153-policy before lifting the ceiling. Denials in any policy layer still win.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-154-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:267:## Session Commands
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-268-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:269:Telegram supports the standard channel session commands:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-270-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-271-| Command | Description |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-272-|---------|-------------|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:273:| `/new` | Start a fresh session for the current chat |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:274:| `/sessions` | List or switch among sessions already bound to the current chat |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:275:| `/attach` | List existing non-cron sessions and rebind one to the current chat |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-276-| `/agent` | List or switch chat agents |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:277:| `/mode` | List or switch temporary session modes |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-278-| `/model` | List or switch models |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:279:| `/approvals` | List pending exec approvals for the current session |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-280-| `/approve N` | Approve the numbered exec request from `/approvals` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-281-| `/deny N` | Deny the numbered exec request from `/approvals` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-282-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:283:`/sessions` is intentionally scoped to the current chat. If you want to bring a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:284:different existing session into the chat, use `/attach` instead. Reattaching a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md:285:session moves that session's channel binding to the current chat, it is not a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-286-copy.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/telegram.md-287-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-154-### How it works
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-155-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md:156:- **Image**: pulled from `ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-157-- **Port**: internal 8080, Fly terminates TLS and routes HTTPS traffic
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md:158:- **Storage**: a Fly Volume mounted at `/data` persists the database, sessions,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md:159:  and memory files
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-160-- **Auto-scaling**: machines stop when idle and start on incoming requests
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-161-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-162-### Custom domain

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-165-fly certs add your-domain.com
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-166-```
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md:178:3. Set image to `ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-179-4. Set the run command: `moltis --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --no-tls`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-180-5. Set environment variables:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-229-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md:231:complete the browser flow when Moltis runs on a remote server — `localhost`

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-248-callback capture fails, Moltis prompts you to paste the callback URL (or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/cloud-deploy.md-249-`code#state`) directly in the terminal. After you log in, tokens are saved to

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:1:# Memory Surfaces
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-3-Moltis has several different places where information can persist. They solve
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:4:different problems, and confusing them leads to very weird debugging sessions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-5-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-6-## Quick Table
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-8-| Surface | Purpose | Lifetime | Scope | Backing store |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-9-|---------|---------|----------|-------|---------------|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:10:| `session_state` | Short-term structured state for a session | Until the session is deleted | One session key | SQLite `session_state` table |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:11:| Managed user profile (`USER.md`) | User name, timezone, and optional location hints | Persistent | Whole workspace | `USER.md` in `data_dir()` plus `[user]` in `moltis.toml` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:12:| Prompt memory (`MEMORY.md`) | High-signal facts injected into the system prompt | Persistent | Agent workspace | `MEMORY.md` in `data_dir()` or `agents/<id>/MEMORY.md` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:13:| Searchable memory (`memory_search`) | Long-term recall without spending prompt tokens | Persistent | Agent workspace | `MEMORY.md`, `memory/*.md`, optional exported session files |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:14:| Managed Files | User-managed documents available to permitted agents | Persistent | Shared across all agent sessions | `<data_dir>/files` on host; `/home/sandbox/files` in supported local containers |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:15:| Session attachments | Files attached to individual chat messages | Session/media retention | A session and message | Session media storage |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:16:| Sandbox workspace mount | Lets sandboxed commands see Moltis files | Only while mounted | Depends on sandbox session/container | Mounted `data_dir()` path |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:17:| Sandbox home (`/home/sandbox`) | Command-side scratch files and tool caches | Depends on `home_persistence` | Shared, per-session, or none | Sandbox home volume/dir |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-18-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:19:## Short-Term Memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-20-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:21:`session_state` is Moltis's short-term memory layer. It is:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:23:- keyed by `(session_key, namespace, key)`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:24:- isolated between sessions
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:25:- available to tools and runtime features that need structured, mutable state
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-26-- not automatically injected into the prompt
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-27-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:28:This is the right place for session-scoped control data, counters, cursors, or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:29:snapshots that should not become part of long-term memory.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-30-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:31:## Long-Term Memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-32-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:33:Long-term memory lives in Markdown files inside the Moltis data directory.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-34-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:35:- Main agent prompt memory:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:36:  `~/.moltis/MEMORY.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:37:- Main agent searchable memory:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:38:  `~/.moltis/memory/*.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:39:- Non-main agent prompt memory:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:40:  `~/.moltis/agents/<agent_id>/MEMORY.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:41:- Non-main agent searchable memory:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:42:  `~/.moltis/agents/<agent_id>/memory/*.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-43-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:44:`USER.md` is not part of agent long-term memory. It is a managed user profile
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-45-surface used for things like name, timezone, and cached location. Moltis also
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-46-stores the canonical user profile in `moltis.toml [user]`, then overlays
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-47-`USER.md` when that file exists.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:49:For `main`, Moltis currently prefers `agents/main/MEMORY.md` if it exists and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:50:falls back to the root `MEMORY.md`. Non-main agents do not fall back to the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-51-root file.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-52-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:53:## Prompt Memory Loading
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-54-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:55:`MEMORY.md` can reach the prompt in two modes:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-56-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-57-```toml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:58:[memory]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-59-style = "hybrid"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-60-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-61-[chat]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:62:prompt_memory_mode = "live-reload"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-63-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-64-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:65:- `hybrid` injects `MEMORY.md` into the prompt and keeps `memory_search`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:66:  `memory_get`, `memory_save`, `memory_forget`, and `memory_delete` available
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:67:- `prompt-only` injects `MEMORY.md` into the prompt, but hides memory tools
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:68:- `search-only` skips prompt injection and relies on memory tools for recall
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:69:- `off` disables both prompt memory injection and memory tools
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:70:- `live-reload` reads `MEMORY.md` again before each turn
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:71:- `frozen-at-session-start` captures the first `MEMORY.md` snapshot seen by a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:72:  session and reuses it for later turns in that same session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-73-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-74-The style and the mode control different things. Style decides whether prompt
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:75:memory exists at all, and whether memory tools are exposed. Mode only matters
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:76:when prompt memory is enabled. Frozen snapshots are stored in `session_state`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:77:so they are session-scoped rather than a process-global cache.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-78-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-79-Defaults today:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-80-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:81:- `memory.style = "hybrid"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:82:- `memory.agent_write_mode = "hybrid"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:83:- `memory.user_profile_write_mode = "explicit-and-auto"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:84:- `memory.backend = "builtin"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:85:- `memory.session_export = "on-new-or-reset"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:86:- `chat.prompt_memory_mode = "live-reload"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-87-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:88:`memory.agent_write_mode` is a third axis:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-89-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:90:- `hybrid` allows agent-authored writes to both `MEMORY.md` and `memory/*.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:91:- `prompt-only` restricts agent-authored writes to `MEMORY.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:92:- `search-only` restricts agent-authored writes to `memory/*.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:93:- `off` disables agent-authored memory mutations, including `memory_save`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:94:  `memory_forget`, `memory_delete`, and the silent pre-compaction memory flush
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-95-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:96:`memory.session_export` is separate again:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-97-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:98:- `on-new-or-reset` exports session transcripts into `memory/sessions/*.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-99-- `off` disables that export hook entirely
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-100-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:101:`memory.user_profile_write_mode` is a fourth axis for the managed `USER.md`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-102-surface:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-103-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-109-## Managed Files and Attachments
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-110-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:111:[Managed Files](managed-files.md) are not memory. Moltis does not automatically
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:112:ingest, index, embed, summarize, search, or inject files from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-113-`<data_dir>/files`. The runtime prompt advertises the Files path and effective
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-114-sandbox access so an agent can deliberately list or read a requested file, but
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:115:the file's contents enter context only after a permitted tool reads them.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-116-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:117:Managed Files are also separate from session attachments. Attachments belong
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:118:to a chat message and session media; uploading one does not copy it into the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:119:managed tree. A Settings > Files upload is shared across all agent sessions
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:120:whose tool and mount policy permits access, including channel-originated
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:121:sessions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-122-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-123-Portable data exports exclude Managed Files by default and include them only
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:124:with an explicit opt-in. Session media is a separate export choice.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-125-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:126:`memory.citations` and `memory.search_merge_strategy` are typed retrieval
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-127-knobs:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-128-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-129-- `citations`: `auto`, `on`, or `off`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:130:- `search_merge_strategy`: `rrf` or `linear`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-131-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-132-Two easy-to-miss interaction rules:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-133-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:134:- builtin embedding knobs such as `memory.provider`, `memory.base_url`,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:135:  `memory.model`, and `memory.api_key` do nothing while
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:136:  `memory.backend = "qmd"`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:137:- `memory.session_export` affects searchable transcript files under
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:138:  `memory/sessions/*.md`, not prompt memory injection
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-139-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:140:The chat UI exposes the active prompt-memory mode in the toolbar and full
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:141:context view. Frozen sessions can also refresh their snapshot manually without
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:142:restarting the session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-143-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-144-## Sandboxes
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-146-Sandboxes have three separate persistence surfaces:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-147-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:148:- Workspace mount, this is how commands can read or write Moltis memory files
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:149:  when `workspace_mount` is not `none`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-150-- Sandbox home, this is `/home/sandbox` and is controlled by
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:151:  `tools.exec.sandbox.home_persistence`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-152-- Managed Files, mounted independently at `/home/sandbox/files` in supported
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-153-  local containers and controlled by `managed_files_mount`
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-156-even though its container path is below `/home/sandbox`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-157-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:158:If a file exists only in `/home/sandbox`, `memory_search` will not index it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:159:If a file exists in the mounted Moltis workspace, it is part of Moltis's
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:160:normal memory surface, regardless of whether the command that wrote it ran in a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-161-sandbox or not.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-162-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-163-A file in `/home/sandbox/files` is likewise not indexed unless it is explicitly
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:164:copied or saved into a configured memory surface.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-165-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:166:With the default `workspace_mount = "ro"`, sandboxed commands may still read
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:167:mounted files such as `MEMORY.md`, but they cannot modify them directly.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:168:Durable long-term memory mutations should still happen through Moltis memory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:169:tools such as `memory_save`, `memory_forget`, and `memory_delete`, not via
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:170:shell redirection inside the sandbox.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-171-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-172-## Between Sandboxes
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-175-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-176-- `off`: nothing in sandbox home persists
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:177:- `session`: sandbox home persists only for that session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:178:- `shared`: sandbox home is reused across sessions/containers that share the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-179-  configured home
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md-180-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:181:This affects `/home/sandbox`, not `MEMORY.md` semantics. Long-term memory is
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/memory-surfaces.md:182:still governed by the mounted Moltis workspace and agent-scoped memory files.
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-120-## Metrics Persistence
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-121-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md:122:Metrics history is persisted to SQLite, so historical data survives server
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-123-restarts. The database is stored at `~/.moltis/metrics.db` (or the configured
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-124-data directory).
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-126-Key features:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-127-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md:128:- **7-day retention**: History is kept for 7 days (60,480 data points at
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-129-  10-second intervals)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-130-- **Automatic cleanup**: Old data is automatically removed hourly
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md:131:- **Startup recovery**: History is loaded from the database when the server
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-132-  starts
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/metrics-and-tracing.md-133-
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-1-# External Agents
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:3:Moltis can bind a chat session to an external CLI coding agent. When a session is bound, `chat.send` persists the user turn in Moltis, sends the prompt and recent session context to the external process, streams the CLI output back to the web UI, and persists the assistant response.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-4-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-5-ACP, the Agent Client Protocol, is a JSON-RPC protocol for connecting editor or coding agents to a host application. Moltis can run ACP-compatible command-line agents as external agents, route their permission prompts through Moltis approvals, and show them alongside provider-backed models in the chat composer selector as `ACP: <agent>`. The canonical ACP agent catalog is https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/agents.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-9-| Kind | Default command | Notes |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-10-|------|-----------------|-------|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:11:| `claude-code` | `claude -p --output-format json` | Print mode with `session_id` capture; later turns add `--resume <id>`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-12-| `codex` | `codex app-server` | Persistent app-server process; Moltis reuses the Codex `threadId` across turns. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:13:| `acp` | `acp` | Persistent ACP JSON-RPC stdio session configured by `[external_agents.agents.acp]`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:14:| `acp-copilot` | `copilot --acp` | Named ACP session shown as `ACP: Copilot` in the chat model selector. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-15-| `acp-codex` | `codex-acp` | Codex via Zed's ACP adapter, shown as `ACP: Codex`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-16-| `acp-claude` | `claude-agent-acp` | Claude Agent SDK via https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp, shown as `ACP: Claude`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-17-| `acp-pi` | `pi-acp` | Pi via the `pi-acp` adapter, shown as `ACP: Pi`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:18:| `acp-opencode` | `opencode acp` | Named ACP session shown as `ACP: opencode` in the chat model selector. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:19:| `acp-gemini` | `gemini --experimental-acp` | Named ACP session shown as `ACP: Gemini` in the chat model selector. |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-49-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:50:Installed ACP agents appear automatically alongside normal models in each chat session's composer selector. Missing commands are hidden, so a fresh install with no ACP agents available continues to show only provider-backed models.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-51-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:52:Default detection only checks whether the named command exists on Moltis' `$PATH`; it does not verify the binary publisher or installation source. Only install ACP agents from trusted sources, keep untrusted directories out of the service `$PATH`, and use explicit `binary = "/absolute/path/to/agent"` overrides when you want to pin the executable Moltis may launch after a user selects that agent for a session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-53-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-130-MiniMax Code is available as the `@minimax-ai/code` npm package. Once its `mcode` binary is on the Moltis service `$PATH`, Moltis detects it automatically and launches `mcode acp` when selected.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-131-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:132:Cursor CLI supports ACP with `agent acp`, but Moltis does not auto-detect it because `agent` is a generic executable name that can collide with unrelated tools. Configure Cursor manually with the generic `acp` entry and an absolute `binary` path if you want to use it.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-171-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-172-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:173:## Select an ACP agent for a session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-174-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:175:The model selector below the chat text field includes installed ACP agents, labeled with the protocol and agent name, such as `ACP: Copilot`. Selecting an ACP entry binds that chat session to the external agent. Select any normal model in the same menu to unbind the ACP agent and return the session to the provider-backed Moltis agent.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-176-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:177:Binding is per session. You can bind one chat session to `ACP: Copilot`, another to `ACP: Claude`, and leave other sessions on the normal Moltis agent.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-178-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:179:Moltis keeps live external sessions in memory while the gateway process is running. Binding, unbinding, clearing, resetting, deleting, or clearing all sessions shuts down the matching live external process. Persisted external session IDs are stored in session metadata for UI/status visibility and for runtimes that can resume from their own IDs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-180-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-181-## ACP permissions and capabilities
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-182-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:183:ACP agents can ask Moltis for permission before running tools. Moltis converts ACP permission requests into normal Moltis approval prompts and selects the matching ACP allow or reject option based on the user decision.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-184-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-185-Moltis advertises ACP file-system and terminal capabilities to agents. File reads and writes are handled through the ACP client bridge. Terminal requests are supported by the ACP bridge but run inside the Moltis gateway environment, so configure `working_dir` and environment variables deliberately.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-187-## Troubleshooting ACP agents
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-188-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:189:- If an ACP agent does not appear in the selector, confirm `[external_agents] enabled = true`, restart Moltis, and verify the configured `binary` exists on `$PATH` or is an absolute path.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:190:- If an ACP entry appears as unavailable, run the configured command manually from the same shell or service environment that starts Moltis.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-191-- If the wrong ACP agent is bound, use the selector below the chat text field and choose the desired `ACP: <agent>` entry; choose a normal model to unbind.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:192:- If the agent needs project-local context, set `working_dir` in that agent's config entry.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-193-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-194-Current limitations:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-195-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md:196:- Claude Code persistence uses print-mode `--resume`; it does not yet keep an interactive PTY alive.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/external-agents.md-197-- Live external processes are not restored automatically after a Moltis gateway restart.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/modes.md-1-# Modes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/modes.md-2-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/modes.md:4:chat agent works right now without creating a new agent, changing memory, or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/modes.md-5-changing sub-agent presets.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:1:# Session State
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:3:Moltis provides a per-session key-value store that allows skills, extensions,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:4:and the agent itself to persist context across messages within a session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-5-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-6-## Overview
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-7-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:8:Session state is scoped to a `(session_key, namespace, key)` triple, backed by
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-9-SQLite. Each entry stores a string value and is automatically timestamped.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-10-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:11:The agent accesses state through the `session_state` tool, which supports five
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-12-operations: `get`, `set`, `delete`, `list`, and `clear`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:14:## Agent Tool
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-15-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:16:The `session_state` tool is registered as a built-in tool and available in every
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:17:session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-18-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-19-### Get a value
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-79-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-80-Every state entry belongs to a namespace. This prevents collisions between
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:81:different skills or extensions using state in the same session. Use your skill
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-82-name as the namespace.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-83-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-84-## Storage
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-85-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:86:State is stored in the `session_state` table in the main SQLite database
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-87-(`moltis.db`). The migration is in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md:88:`crates/sessions/migrations/20260205120000_session_state.sql`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-89-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/session-state.md-90-```admonish tip

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-7-## Quick Start

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-10-docker run -d \

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-16-  -v moltis-data:/home/moltis/.moltis \
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-17-  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:18:  ghcr.io/moltis-org/moltis:latest
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-19-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-20-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:21:Open https://localhost:13131 in your browser and configure your LLM provider to start chatting.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-23-For unattended bootstraps, add `MOLTIS_TOKEN`, `MOLTIS_PROVIDER`, and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-24-`MOLTIS_API_KEY` before first start. That pre-configures auth plus one LLM
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:25:provider so you can skip the browser setup wizard entirely.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-26-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-27-### Ports

runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-35-### Trusting the TLS certificate
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-36-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:37:Moltis generates a self-signed CA on first run. Browsers will show a security
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-38-warning until you trust this CA. Port 13132 serves the certificate over plain
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-39-HTTP so you can download it:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-40-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:41:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-42-# Download the CA certificate
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-43-curl -o moltis-ca.pem http://localhost:13132/certs/ca.pem
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-52-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-53-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:54:After trusting the CA, restart your browser. The warning will not appear again
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-55-(the CA persists in the mounted config volume).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-56-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-59-host name, and sometimes an inferred non-loopback bind IP. It does not make a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-60-certificate valid for an arbitrary public VPS IP address or hosting-provider
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:61:domain. Browsers still reject those targets with a certificate name mismatch if
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-62-they are not present in the certificate SAN list. IP-address URLs require an IP
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-63-SAN. For direct `https://<public-ip>:13131` access, set `tls.public_ip` to that
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-83-Docker's default bridge networking rewrites the request's apparent source
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-84-address, so this "no auth needed" convenience does not apply automatically
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:85:inside a container even when the browser genuinely is on the same machine
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-86-— see [Docker and check 4](authentication.md#docker-and-check-4) for why,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-87-and the `MOLTIS_TRUST_DOCKER_LOOPBACK` opt-in if you've confirmed your own
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-88-port publish is loopback-only.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-89-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md:90:~~~bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-91-docker logs moltis
runtime/cde-20260926/external/moltis-docs/docs/src/docker.md-92-~~~
